summary: Say how many are in a briefly shown group of up to 10 without counting (subitizing).
Count objects one-to-one and know the last number counted is how many there are.
Know each next number in the count means one more.
Given a number from 1 to 20, count out that many objects.
Count up to 20 objects in a line, array or circle, or up to 10 scattered.
Count aloud forward and backward from any number within 20.
Count aloud by ones and tens to 100, crossing decades correctly (89 to 90).
Write and name numbers 0 to 20 and use a numeral for a counted group.
Compare two groups of up to 20 objects with fewer than, more than, the same as.
Show numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones with models, drawings or equations.
Show and explain adding as putting together and subtracting as taking apart, with objects or equations.
Break apart and put together numbers up to 10 as pairs in more than one way.
Find the number that makes 10 with a given number from 1 to 9 and show it.
Add and subtract within 5 quickly, flexibly and accurately.
Solve real addition and subtraction problems within 10 using objects, drawings or equations.
Name circles, triangles, squares and rectangles in any size or position (hexagons not listed).
Name spheres, cubes, cylinders and cones in any size or position.
Describe where shapes are using words like above, below, in front of, behind, next to.
Make shapes from materials and describe features such as number of sides or corners.
Put simple shapes together to make larger shapes.
Describe things you can measure on real objects, such as length, capacity and weight.
Directly compare two objects to say which is longer, heavier or holds more.
Name pennies, nickels and dimes and know their values.
Name the parts of digital and analog clocks and tell time to the hour.
Sort and classify objects by size, shape, color or other features (no counting categories required).
Find the object that does not belong in a group and explain why.
Say how many are in a briefly shown group of up to 20 without counting.
Count aloud by ones and tens within 120, starting from any number.
Count on and back within 120, linking each step to adding or removing one object.
Write the numeral for a set of up to 120 objects.
Understand skip-counting patterns by 2s, 5s and 10s.
Understand 10 as a bundle of ten ones and two-digit numbers as tens and ones.
Compare two-digit numbers with words and <, >, = and justify using tens and ones.
Add and subtract within 20 using strategies like counting on, making ten and doubles.
Add and subtract within 10 quickly, flexibly and accurately.
Find the difference between two multiples of 10 (10 to 90) and write the equation.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number mentally and explain.
Add within 100 (two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of ten) using place value; explain.
When adding two-digit numbers, add tens to tens and ones to ones, sometimes making a ten.
Subtract multiples of ten from any two-digit number with models and explain (CCSS: multiples of ten only).
Use the equal sign to decide if equations are true and give examples of true ones.
Solve subtraction by thinking of a related addition fact.
Find the missing whole number in an addition or subtraction equation.
Use the commutative property and composing or decomposing numbers as addition and subtraction strategies.
Solve problems adding three whole numbers with a total of 20 or less.
Solve real add and subtract problems within 20 of all types, unknown in any position.
Write a real-world story problem to match a given addition or subtraction equation within 20.
Find geometric features of rhombi, trapezoids and hexagons in any position or size.
Find geometric features of cones, cylinders, cubes and rectangular prisms in any position or size.
Describe lines and sides of shapes as parallel or not parallel.
Split circles and rectangles into two or four equal parts named halves and fourths.
Measure length with copies of a non-standard unit laid end to end.
Order three objects by length, comparing directly or by using a third object.
Know a dime equals ten pennies, link to tens and ones, and solve dime-penny problems with cents.
Count sets of one coin type (pennies, nickels or dimes) by 1s, 5s or 10s.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Collect, organize and show data in up to three categories with a picture graph.
Answer questions about a picture graph: total, each category, how many more or fewer.
Quickly tell how many are in a briefly shown structured group using groups and place value.
Count within 1,000, skip counting by 5s, 10s and 100s from different starting multiples.
Read and write numbers 0 to 1,000 in standard, word and expanded form.
Understand 100 as ten tens and three-digit numbers as hundreds, tens and ones.
Compare three-digit numbers with <, =, > and justify using place values.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently.
Add and subtract within 100 using place value, properties, inverse relationships and algorithms.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from numbers 100 to 900.
Add up to three two-digit numbers using place value and properties (CCSS allows four).
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models, drawings and place-value strategies.
Solve real add and subtract problems within 100 of all types, unknowns anywhere.
Write one-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100 with the unknown in any position.
Use repeated addition to total an array up to 5 by 5 and write an equation.
Tell if a group of 0 to 20 objects is even or odd by pairing or equal parts.
Identify the flat faces of solid shapes and count their edges, faces and vertices.
Recognize and draw shapes with given numbers of sides, angles and vertices, through hexagons.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths and describe the parts.
Know equal parts of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
Measure an object with two different units and explain how the results relate to unit size.
Find how much longer one object is than another in inches/feet or centimeters/meters.
Pick and use the right tools to measure length.
Measure and estimate lengths in whole inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Show whole numbers on a number line and use it to add and subtract within 100.
Solve length problems in one unit with addition and subtraction within 100.
Solve problems with dollar bills and coins, using $ and cent signs correctly.
Tell and write time to five minutes on analog and digital clocks with a.m. and p.m.
Ask questions to gather data and show it in scaled picture graphs with up to four categories.
Ask questions to gather data and show it in bar graphs with up to four categories.
Make a line plot of a whole-number data set.
Read scaled picture graphs or bar graphs (up to four categories) to solve one-step comparisons.
Read, write and show numbers up to 10,000 in standard and expanded form with models.
Compare whole numbers up to 10,000 using number lines and reasoning, and justify.
Split shapes into equal areas and name each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
Find parts of a whole using fraction models.
Show and understand a fraction as a point on a number line.
Show and identify equivalent fractions with pictures, manipulatives and number lines.
Explain whole numbers as fractions and find fractions equal to whole numbers.
Compare and order fractions with the same numerator or denominator by reasoning about size.
Add and subtract whole numbers up to four digits, with or without regrouping (CCSS: within 1,000).
Check whether sums and differences make sense using estimation and number sense.
Write and solve one-step equations for real problems with any operation and unknown start, change or result.
Interpret and solve two-step real problems with whole numbers and the four operations.
Use commutative, associative, distributive, identity and zero properties to multiply and divide.
Explain multiplication and division and how they relate using drawings, arrays, groups and number lines.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently using strategies and properties.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 from 10 to 90.
Sort quadrilaterals into categories by their features (no drawing of non-examples).
Solve real perimeter problems given side lengths, or given perimeter with a missing side.
Measure areas by counting square units with concrete and pictured models.
Find rectangle area by tiling, show area adds, and see it matches multiplying the sides.
Choose tools and units to solve problems on length, weight, mass, liquid volume and capacity.
Estimate and measure length to the nearest half inch, quarter inch and centimeter.
Tell and write time to the minute on analog and digital clocks.
Solve real problems adding and subtracting time intervals and finding elapsed time.
Make scaled picture and bar graphs for data with more than four categories.
Collect data and show it on line plots marked in halves and whole units.
Analyze data and make simple statements from picture graphs, line plots and bar graphs.
Read, write and show whole numbers to 1,000,000 and decimals to hundredths in several forms.
Compare whole numbers to 1,000,000 and decimals to hundredths and justify.
Know a digit is worth ten times what it is worth one place to the right.
Write fractions with denominator 10 or 100 as decimals, like 43/100 = 0.43.
Show with models how mixed numbers and fractions greater than one are equivalent.
Explain how multiplying by a fraction equal to 1 makes equivalent fractions.
Compare and order fractions with unlike numerators or denominators using benchmarks or equivalence.
Break a fraction into a sum of same-denominator fractions in more than one way.
Explain adding and subtracting like-denominator fractions with models and properties.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.
Solve real problems adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number using models and properties.
Decide if a whole number up to 100 is a multiple of a one-digit number.
Find factors of numbers up to 100 and classify them as prime or composite.
Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with an algorithm.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit divisors, with or without remainders.
Check whether products and quotients make sense using estimation and number sense.
Write a simple expression or equation with a variable for an unknown in a real situation.
Solve one- and two-step real problems with all four operations, remainders and a letter unknown.
Identify, draw and describe points, lines, segments, rays, angles, and parallel, perpendicular, intersecting lines.
Classify angles as acute, obtuse or right and justify.
Justify classifying shapes by parallel or perpendicular lines or by specific angles.
Recognize, draw and justify lines of symmetry in flat shapes.
Choose tools, operations and units to solve problems on time, length, weight, mass and capacity.
Judge whether measurements of time, length, weight, mass, capacity or angles are reasonable.
Convert from a larger unit to a smaller one in customary and metric systems.
Measure angles with a protractor and relate benchmark angles to turns of a circle.
Treat angle measures as additive to find unknown angles in a diagram.
Use rectangle perimeter and area formulas to solve real problems.
Collect data and make line plots marked in wholes, halves, fourths or eighths.
Solve problems adding or subtracting fractions using data from line plots.
Read, write and show whole numbers and decimals to thousandths in standard and expanded form.
Know a digit is worth one tenth of what it is worth one place to the left.
Use whole-number exponents to write powers of 10.
Write common fractions and decimals in equivalent forms, such as halves, fourths, fifths, tenths.
Compare whole numbers, fractions, mixed numbers and decimals to thousandths and justify.
Understand a fraction as the numerator divided by the denominator.
Multiply whole numbers by fractions and fractions by fractions, including mixed numbers, with models.
Divide a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction.
Solve real problems adding, subtracting and multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators, no simplifying required.
Solve real problems dividing unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with place-value strategies or algorithms.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers with an algorithm.
Divide four-digit numbers by two-digit divisors, with or without remainders.
Justify whether answers with whole numbers, fractions and decimals are reasonable.
Simplify real numerical or algebraic expressions using order of operations, without exponents.
Identify and describe the faces, edges and vertices of rectangular prisms.
Know volume is a feature of solid figures measured in cubic units.
Justify classifying flat figures in a hierarchy by their properties.
Identify the origin, x-axis and y-axis of the coordinate plane.
Graph and name first-quadrant points from whole-number ordered pairs.
Make ordered pairs from real rules or patterns, graph them and interpret the coordinates.
Convert between larger and smaller units in customary and metric systems in real problems.
Find areas of rectangles with fraction sides by tiling and show it matches multiplying.
Multiply fractional side lengths for rectangle areas and show fraction products as areas.
Measure rectangular prism volume by counting cubic units with concrete models.
Find prism volume with unit cubes, show volume adds, and match it to base times height.
Use the formulas l x w x h and B x h for real prism volume problems.
Show, analyze and solve problems with data in tables or line plots of whole numbers and fractions.

state_code: # SOURCES (Nebraska's College and Career Ready Standards for Mathematics, approved 2022-09-02; NDE page checked 2026-10-01 still lists them as current)
# - ccss mappings start from the NDE crosswalk; I changed them where the crosswalk looked off (listed under UNSURE).
# STRANDS (code = grade.STRAND.standard.indicator; rows are the lettered indicators)
# - N = Number (K-2 includes "Number and Algebraic Relationships", e.g. K.N.4, 1.N.5, 2.N.5)
# - A = Algebra (K-2 say "see Number"; coded A indicators start in grade 3)
# - G = Geometry (shapes, measurement, time and money, area/perimeter/volume, coordinate geometry)
# - D = Data (D.1 data collection, D.2 analyze data; 5.D.1 has no indicators)
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED OR NOT FOUND
# - 1.G.A.2 (compose shapes): no grade 1 indicator (composing is K.G.1.e).
# - 3.NBT.A.1, 4.NBT.A.3, 5.NBT.A.4 (rounding): no rounding indicators in K-5; only estimation for reasonableness.
# - 4.OA.A.1, 4.OA.A.2 (multiplicative comparison): not named (NDE crosswalk links 4.OA.A.2 to 4.A.1.f).
# - K.CC.C.7 (compare written numerals): NE compares groups only.
# - K.G.A.3 (flat vs solid): not stated. K.G.1.a omits hexagons.
# - 2.NBT.B.6: three addends instead of four. 3.G.A.1: no drawing of non-examples.
# - 1.OA.D.7: only true equations named; 1.OA.B.3: commutative only.
# - New: subitizing K-2 (K.N.1.a, 1.N.1.a, 2.N.1.a), finding the item that does not belong (K.D.1.b), writing story problems (1.N.5.g, 2.N.5.b),
#   faces/edges/vertices of solids (2.G.1.a, 5.G.1.a), fraction-decimal equivalents (5.N.2.a), justifying reasonableness (5.A.1.c).
# - Moved earlier: coins and clocks in K, coins in grade 1, skip counting in grade 1, parallel sides in grade 1, numbers to 10,000 in grade 3.
# - Extras inside matched rows: counting backward (K.N.2.e, 1.N.2.b), identity/zero properties (3.A.1.e), intersecting lines (4.G.1.a), algorithms in grade 2 (2.N.4.b).
# - The PDF prints 3.G.1.a as "3.G.1.1"; the 2024 Excel and the crosswalk use 3.G.1.a, used here.
